Cadre 3.0.0 is a ground-up simplification of the harness around a
human-governed, Git-aware create-to-archive lifecycle for OpenAI Codex and
Claude Code. Compared with 2.2.0, it replaces the generic packet workflow and
multi-runtime package with ten native skills, purpose-built typed MCP tools,
immutable templates, resumable journals, and one self-contained installer.

## Highlights

- **Ten native workflows.** `create`, `track`, `implement`, `review`, `revise`,
  `archive`, `refresh`, `revert`, `status`, and `wisp` replace the former
  19-command setup/newtrack/ship/land/release family. Codex and Claude discover
  the same workflow set through their native plugin surfaces.
- **A smaller runtime contract.** The published `cadre-ai` package now exposes
  one executable and two self-contained ESM bundles: `dist/cadre-cli.mjs` and
  `dist/cadre-mcp.mjs`. The MCP server provides 35 typed, purpose-built tools
  for project state, tracks, governance, execution, templates, and worktrees.
- **Approved state, not copied runtime.** Initialized projects keep mutable,
  human-approved state under `.cadre/`; skills, agents, runtime code, and the
  immutable `v1` template catalog stay in the installed plugin.
- **Resumable human governance.** Digest-gated preview/apply operations and
  journals cover creation, tracking, execution, revision, review remediation,
  refresh, revert, and archive. Recovery reconciles Git and Cadre state instead
  of discarding or silently replaying work.
- **Hybrid parallel execution.** One main scheduler allocates a global worker
  bound across dependency-ready phases and task waves. A phase may hand off at
  clean checkpoints between a phase worker and task-worker fan-out, with
  separate worktrees, distinct task commits, serialized integration, and
  ancestry-proven cleanup.
- **Native dual-client installation.** The local marketplace installs
  `cadre@cadre` at user scope for Codex and Claude, configures the packaged MCP
  path for each client, and applies narrow MCP approval without replacing
  unrelated user settings.
- **Rebuilt documentation.** The public docs now match the 3.0 runtime and add
  a parallel-execution walkthrough, worker sizing guidance, Codex/Claude
  command switchers with syntax highlighting, and a session-scoped
  System/Light/Dark theme control. Polyrepo mode is documented as coming soon.

## Compared with 2.2.0

| Area | 2.2.0 | 3.0.0 |
|---|---|---|
| Project control plane | `cadre/` state mixed with the 2.x schema and projections | Approved mutable state under `.cadre/`; runtime and templates remain plugin-owned |
| Workflow surface | 19 explicit commands backed by generic workflow packets | 10 native lifecycle skills backed by purpose-built operations |
| MCP boundary | Three generic public tools with nested packet continuations | 35 typed tools for exact Cadre capabilities |
| Runtime/package | CommonJS runtime, five published binaries, runtime dependencies spread across scripts | Two self-contained ESM bundles and one `cadre-ai` executable |
| Supported clients | Codex, Claude Code, Copilot, and Antigravity paths | Native Codex and Claude Code plugins only |
| Planning and execution | Phase/task execution used the legacy parallel state model | Validated dependency DAGs, derived manual barriers, global worker bounds, and clean phase/task handoffs |
| Governance | Atomic canonical/projection review sessions | Digest-gated previews and resumable journals across the complete lifecycle and Git integration |
| Templates and learning | Legacy JSON catalogs, project skills, formulas, and team/provider layers | Immutable Markdown-first `v1` templates, dependency-phase learning, and archive-time durable pattern distillation |
| Distribution license | Apache-2.0 | MIT |

The comparison spans 80 commits and 367 files, with 11,426 insertions and
81,271 deletions. Most deletions remove the retired 2.x runtime, compatibility
layers, generated command sources, provider/team tooling, LSP/DAP integration,
and legacy template catalogs rather than reducing the supported 3.0 lifecycle.

## Breaking migration from 2.x

Cadre 3.0 does not migrate a 2.x project in place.

- Use the `cadre-ai` executable; the `cadre` alias is removed.
- Do not rename `cadre/` to `.cadre/`. The state schemas and lifecycle differ.
- Replace saved 2.x commands with the corresponding 3.0 native workflow.
- Custom clients must stop invoking `cadre_workflow`, `cadre_action`, or
  `cadre_read`; those generic packet tools no longer exist.
- Copilot, Antigravity, provider evidence, team boards, merge trains, project
  skills, formulas, LSP/DAP, and polyrepo orchestration are not part of 3.0.
- Preserve existing 2.x state and Git history, then choose a deliberate fresh
  `.cadre/` initialization or migration strategy before running `create`.

Polyrepo mode is planned for a later release.

## Install or upgrade

```bash
npm install -g cadre-ai@3.0.0
cadre-ai doctor
cadre-ai install --target all --scope user
```

Start a new Codex conversation and run `/reload-plugins` in Claude Code after
installation.

- Codex launches `./dist/cadre-mcp.mjs`; Claude launches
  `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/dist/cadre-mcp.mjs`; both retain the intended narrow
